title: opum-workflow hook writes provenance-corrupting notes onto unrelated tasks
summary: hooks/flush-state.sh attributes its SessionEnd/PreCompact tracker note to 'whichever task is the sole In Progress one' (opum_active_task in _lib.sh), not to the task the ending session actually worked on. OMARK-23's fix (withhold the note on a clean, fully-pushed tree) only reduces how often a note fires; it does not change which task receives it when one does. The heuristic fails in both directions at once: a repo with a long-lived blocked task as its sole In Progress item gets EVERY unrelated session's note glued onto that one task, and a repo with two or more legitimately concurrent In Progress tasks (lore-web's normal state -- LWEB-55 is saws's work, LWEB-67 is theirs) gets no note written for either, silently, every time. Observed directly: lore-web's own commit d4744dc says outright 'The opum-workflow write hook appends a note to whichever task is the sole In Progress one; here that's LWEB-55 (saws's)' -- three of LWEB-55's nine hook-written notes came from sessions working on entirely unrelated tasks while LWEB-55 sat blocked. This is worse than OMARK-23's dilution bug: OMARK-23 made task records noisy; this makes them WRONG. A committed, durable tracker record on LWEB-55 now carries notes that read as evidence of activity on LWEB-55 to anyone auditing it later, when the sessions that wrote them were doing unrelated work.

acceptanceCriteria.text: State the two-sided failure precisely as a design constraint any fix must satisfy: the fix must correctly attribute (or correctly withhold) a note both when the repo has exactly one In Progress task that is not the ending session's own work, and when the repo has two or more legitimately concurrent In Progress tasks and the session's own one is unambiguous to the session even though it is ambiguous to a hook re-deriving state from `quest task list` alone.

Evaluate at least the session-scoped-claim-marker approach recorded in this task's implementation notes (below) against the DIRTY_LIST/modifiedFiles correlation approach also recorded there, and choose one, before writing code -- this is a provenance-correctness question, not a redundancy question, and deserves a deliberate design pass rather than the smallest patch that passes a test.

Whatever ships must not regress OMARK-23: a note must still fire only when the repository has something uncommitted or unpushed for it to protect, and the unconditional cursor write must stay unaffected either way.

Decide, explicitly and in writing on this task, whether pre-existing corrupted notes (LWEB-55's nine, named here as the evidence trail) are worth annotating or leaving as-is with a pointer to this task -- silently leaving them uncorrected without saying so is not an acceptable default.

implementationNotes: Filed by opum-agent (orchestrator) ruling, 2026-09-09: this is more serious than OMARK-23's dilution bug and should not sit as a note on a task that is about to close. Also flagged: this interacts badly with lore-web's own legitimate two-In-Progress state (LWEB-55 is saws's work, LWEB-67 is theirs) -- a repo with two In Progress tasks gets no note at all under the current 'exactly one' guard, and a repo with one blocked task gets everyone's. Both are the same root defect from opposite sides.

My own read, captured while the context from OMARK-23 is fresh, of what a real fix would take -- not a ruling, a starting point for whoever picks this up: flush-state.sh currently has no notion of 'the task THIS session worked on'; opum_active_task derives its answer entirely from live `quest task list --status "In Progress"` output at hook-fire time, which is repo-wide state, not session-scoped state. Two candidate directions: (a) SESSION-SCOPED CLAIM MARKER -- when a session calls `quest task edit <id> --status "In Progress"` itself (the existing opum-sdlc/quest-writes 'Claim' step), also drop a small session-local marker (an env var set for the session's lifetime is not available to a hook process across separate invocations, so this likely needs a file under something like .claude/ naming the id, written at claim time and read -- not re-derived -- by flush-state.sh); the hook then writes to that claimed id specifically, or writes nothing if the session's own claim marker is absent or stale, rather than falling back to a fleet-wide 'the sole one' guess. This directly fixes both failure directions: an unclaimed session writes nothing (no more gluing onto an unrelated blocked task), and two concurrent sessions each write to their own correctly-claimed task (no more silent nothing under real concurrency). Costs: a new piece of session-local state to keep fresh and clean up, and it does nothing for a session that does real work without ever formally claiming a task -- which opum-sdlc already discourages but does not technically prevent for small chores. (b) FILE-PATH CORRELATION -- compare DIRTY_LIST's changed paths against each In Progress task's `modifiedFiles` field and attribute the note to whichever task's declared files overlap. Rejected in my own read as the weaker option: `modifiedFiles` is optional and not consistently populated (this session's own OMARK-21/22/23 work never set it), a tracker-only chore touching only `.quest/tasks/*.json` has no source files to correlate against anything, and a session touching files that happen to overlap two tasks' declared lists has no principled tiebreak. (a) is very likely the right direction; recorded here so the next implementer does not have to rediscover it.

Interim mitigation already in force fleet-wide for OMARK-23 also covers this task's blast radius: nobody opens a PR whose entire content is a hook-written note. That does not stop a note from landing on the wrong task when a substantive commit does need a PR anyway -- this task is not mitigated the way OMARK-23 was, only reduced in frequency by it.

Related interaction, recorded here per opum-agent's flag on OMARK-23: whatever this task's eventual fix looks like (session-scoped claim marker is the leading candidate per this task's own notes) will also change how and when the hook writes a tracker note, which touches the same 'uncommitted tracker state reads as normal' habit that OMARK-28 documents. Not a reason to change this task's scope -- OMARK-28 is the place the rule itself gets written -- but worth the implementer knowing the interim mitigation's side effect exists before touching the same hook mechanism again.

AC0 -- the failure stated as a design constraint (verified against opum-workflow 0.8.2's hooks/_lib.sh:225-231 and hooks/flush-state.sh:72-85, both read directly from the installed cache at ~/.claude/plugins/cache/opum-fleet/opum-workflow/0.8.2/, so the defect described here is confirmed still present in the currently-installed version, not stale from 2026-09-09): opum_active_task derives ACTIVE purely from a repo-wide `quest task list --status "In Progress" --json` snapshot at hook-fire time, with no session-scoped signal at all. flush-state.sh then branches only on ACTIVE's shape (empty / space-containing / exactly-one), never on whether ACTIVE is the ending session's own work. A correct fix must satisfy both sides at once: (1) exactly one In Progress task that is NOT the ending session's own -- must withhold, not glue; (2) two-plus legitimately concurrent In Progress tasks, each unambiguous to its own session -- must attribute correctly to each session's own task, not withhold for both. A fix that only picks-under-ambiguity still fails (2): a hook re-deriving state from quest task list alone cannot tell which of N concurrent tasks belongs to the exiting session without a session-scoped signal it does not currently have.

AC1 -- evaluated both candidates against opum-workflow's own current code, not just this task's 2026-09-09 notes. (a) SESSION-SCOPED CLAIM MARKER: this fleet already ships the identical pattern for an analogous problem -- opum_marker_path (_lib.sh:141-145) writes a per-session file under .claude/handovers/running-plugin-root[.$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID], gitignored fleet-wide, keyed by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID when present and falling back to an unsuffixed name when absent on both sides (OFLE-54's fix for two sessions sharing a project). Extending this exact mechanism -- write a claimed-task-id marker at the moment a session runs quest task start / quest task edit --status In Progress on its own behalf, then have flush-state.sh READ (not re-derive) that marker instead of calling opum_active_task -- directly satisfies both sides of AC0: an unclaimed session's marker is absent, so it writes nothing; two concurrent sessions each hold their own marker file, so each writes to its own task. (b) DIRTY_LIST / modifiedFiles CORRELATION: rejected on verified evidence, not just the prior notes' anecdote -- opum-marketplace's own tracker has 22 tasks and I confirmed 0 of 22 have modifiedFiles populated at all (grep across .quest/tasks/*.json, zero hits). There is nothing to correlate against in the one repo checkable directly, and a tracker/docs-only chore has no source files to correlate in the first place. DECISION: (a), the session-scoped claim marker, extending the existing opum_marker_path pattern rather than inventing a new one.

AC2 -- verified non-regression path against the current guard (flush-state.sh:72-85): OMARK-23's clean-tree guard (skip when DIRTY=0 and nothing unpushed) decides WHETHER a write happens at all and is orthogonal to WHICH task id it targets. Approach (a) only changes the target-id resolution (session's own claim marker, read-not-derived) inside the same guarded branch; it does not touch the guard itself or the unconditional cursor write in step 2. The implementer should keep the guard exactly where it is and swap only the ACTIVE-id source.

AC3 -- decision, in writing: leave LWEB-55's nine existing hook-written notes as-is, do not edit or remove any of them, and add ONE new note on LWEB-55 (to be written by a lore-web or opum-fleet session, since opum-marketplace has no write authority over a sibling's tracker) pointing at this task as the explanation for the anomalous notes. Reasoning: a tracker note is meant to be a durable, append-only record; editing or deleting past entries to correct them would itself be the same class of provenance corruption this task exists to stop, just committed in the other direction. An explanatory pointer preserves the historical record, including its own mistake, while telling a future auditor what happened and why. This is a recommendation for whoever owns LWEB-55's tracker, not an action opum-marketplace can take itself.
